title: Greetings & Introductions
description: Master the essentials of greeting people, introducing yourself, and handling basic social interactions in Spanish. Learn formal and informal expressions, time-based greetings, and how to ask about someone's well-being.

grammar.title: Ser — Identity, Origin, Profession
grammar.content:
Use SER to express who you are, where you're from, and what you do.

Conjugation: yo soy, tú eres, él/ella es, nosotros somos, vosotros sois, ellos son

- Soy [name]. (I'm [name].)
- Soy de [country/city]. (I'm from [country/city].)
- Soy [profession]. (I'm a [profession].)
- Es [name]. (He/She is [name].)

NO article before profession:
- Soy ingeniero. (NOT Soy el ingeniero)
- Ella es médica.

With adjectives, you DO use the article:
- Es un buen médico. (He's a good doctor.)
- Soy una persona feliz. (I'm a happy person.)
examples:
Soy Sergiu. (I'm Sergiu.)
Soy de Valencia. (I'm from Valencia.)
Soy ingeniero. (I'm an engineer.)
Ella es médica. (She's a doctor.)
Nosotros somos estudiantes. (We're students.)

Él es de España. (He's from Spain.)
Soy programador. (I'm a programmer.)
Ella es mi esposa. (She's my wife.)

grammar.title: Estar — Current State/Condition
grammar.content:
Use ESTAR to express how you're feeling RIGHT NOW (temporary state).

Conjugation: yo estoy, tú estás, él/ella está, nosotros estamos, vosotros estáis, ellos están

- ¿Cómo estás? (How are you?)
- Estoy bien. (I'm fine.)
- Estoy cansado/a. (I'm tired.)
- Estoy feliz/triste. (I'm happy/sad.)

SER vs ESTAR:
- Soy feliz = I'm a happy person (identity)
- Estoy feliz = I'm happy right now (current state)

Estar + adjective must match gender:
- Estoy cansado (m) / cansada (f)
- Estoy aburrido (m) / aburrida (f)
examples:
¿Cómo estás? — Estoy bien. (How are you? — I'm fine.)
Estoy cansado. (I'm tired.)
Ella está feliz. (She's happy.)
Estamos bien, gracias. (We're fine, thanks.)

Estoy aburrido. (I'm bored.)
¿Cómo está usted? — Estoy bien, gracias. (How are you? — I'm fine, thanks.)

grammar.title: Present Tense: -AR Verbs (Regular)
grammar.content:
Regular -AR verbs follow this pattern:

Remove -AR, add endings: -o, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an

Example: HABlar (to speak)
- yo hablo (I speak)
- tú hablas (you speak informal)
- él/ella habla (he/she speaks)
- nosotros hablamos (we speak)
- vosotros habláis (you speak plural, Spain)
- ellos hablan (they speak)

Common -AR verbs:
- hablar (to speak)
- llamar (to call)
- trabajar (to work)
- estudiar (to study)
- caminar (to walk)
- visitar (to visit)
- necesitar (to need)
- querer (to want — stem-changing e→ie)
examples:
Hablo español. (I speak Spanish.)
Tú hablas inglés. (You speak English.)
¿Hablas francés? (Do you speak French?)
Nosotros hablamos inglés. (We speak English.)
Ella trabaja aquí. (She works here.)
Yo estudio español. (I study Spanish.)

¿Cómo te llamas? — Me llamo Ana. (What's your name? — My name is Ana.)
Ella necesita ayuda. (She needs help.)
Nosotros visitamos museos. (We visit museums.)

grammar.title: Present Tense: -ER Verbs (Regular)
grammar.content:
Regular -ER verbs follow this pattern:

Remove -ER, add endings: -o, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en

Example: COMER (to eat)
- yo como (I eat)
- tú comes (you eat)
- él/ella come (he/she eats)
- nosotros comemos (we eat)
- vosotros coméis (you eat plural, Spain)
- ellos comen (they eat)

Common -ER verbs:
- comer (to eat)
- leer (to read)
- correr (to run)
- conocer (to know/meet)
- poner (to put — irregular yo form)
- tener (to have — irregular)
- venir (to come — irregular)

Conocer + person = to meet for the first time
- Conozco a María. (I met Maria.)
Conocer + thing = to be familiar with
- Conozco Madrid. (I know Madrid.)
examples:
Como paella. (I eat paella.)
Tú lees libros. (You read books.)
Ella come arroz. (She eats rice.)
Nosotros comemos juntos. (We eat together.)
Conozco a tu amigo. (I know your friend.)

Leo mucho. (I read a lot.)
Corro todos los días. (I run every day.)
Conozco esta ciudad. (I know this city.)

grammar.title: Present Tense: -IR Verbs (Regular)
grammar.content:
Regular -IR verbs follow this pattern:

Remove -IR, add endings: -o, -es, -e, -imos, -ís, -en

Example: VIVIR (to live)
- yo vivo (I live)
- tú vives (you live)
- él/ella vive (he/she lives)
- nosotros vivimos (we live)
- vosotros vivís (you live plural, Spain)
- ellos viven (they live)

Common -IR verbs:
- vivir (to live)
- escribir (to write)
- abrir (to open)
- decidir (to decide)
- salir (to leave/go out — yo form: salgo)
- pedir (to ask for — stem-changing e→i)
- dormir (to sleep — stem-changing o→ue)
- servir (to serve — stem-changing e→ie)
examples:
Vivo en Valencia. (I live in Valencia.)
Tú vives aquí. (You live here.)
Ella vive en Madrid. (She lives in Madrid.)
Nosotros vivimos juntos. (We live together.)
Escribo cartas. (I write letters.)
Abro la puerta. (I open the door.)

Salgo temprano. (I leave early.)
Pedimos agua. (We ask for water.)
Duermo ocho horas. (I sleep eight hours.)

grammar.title: Gender Agreement for Nationalities
grammar.content:
Spanish nationalities change form for gender:

Masculine: -o → Femenine: -a
- español/española (Spanish)
- americano/americana (American)
- inglés/inglesa (English)
- francés/francesa (French)
- alemán/alemana (German)

Some nationalities are invariable (same for both genders):
- japonés/japonesa (Japanese — but has -a form)
- chino/china (Chinese — but has -a form)
- portugués/portuguesa (Portuguese — but has -a form)

INVARIAIBLE (same form):
- catalán/catalana (Catalan — has -a)
- italiano/italiana (Italian — has -a)
- brasileño/brasileña (Brazilian — has -a)

Actually, MOST have both forms. Invariable ones:
- árabe (Arab)
- turco/turca (Turkish — has -a)
- neerlandés/neerlandesa (Dutch)

The rule: if it ends in -o, change to -a for feminine.
examples:
Soy español. (I'm Spanish — male speaker)
Soy española. (I'm Spanish — female speaker)
Él es americano. (He's American.)
Ella es americana. (She's American.)
Soy inglés. (I'm English — male speaker)
Ella es inglesa. (She's English — female speaker)

Ellos son españoles. (They're Spanish — mixed or male group)
Ellas son españolas. (They're Spanish — all female)
¿De dónde eres? — Soy de Valencia.

pronunciation.title: Spanish Vowels — Always Consistent
pronunciation.content:
Spanish has 5 vowel sounds, and they NEVER change. Unlike English where 'a' can be 'ay' (cake) or 'ah' (cat), Spanish vowels are always the same:

A = ah (like in 'father')
E = eh (like in 'bed')
I = ee (like in 'see')
O = oh (like in 'go')
U = oo (like in 'food')

Examples:
- hola = OH-lah (always 'oh')
- casa = KAH-sah (always 'ah')
- mesa = MEH-sah (always 'eh')
- vida = BEE-dah (always 'ee')
- luna = LOO-nah (always 'oo')

This makes Spanish pronunciation much easier than English!
examples:
hola = OH-lah
buenos días = BWEH-nohs DEE-ahs
buenas tardes = BWEH-nahs TAR-dehs
gracias = GRAH-see-ahs
adiós = ah-DEE-ohs

pronunciation.title: The Spanish 'J' — Like English 'H'
pronunciation.content:
The letter J in Spanish is pronounced like a strong English 'H' (but more guttural):

- jó = HOH (like 'hoe')
- jar = HAHr (like 'harp' without the p)
- ja = HAH (like 'ha')
- je = HEH (like 'hey' without y)
- ji = HEE (like 'he')
- jo = HOH (like 'ho')
- ju = HOO (like 'who')

Examples:
- gracias = GRAH-see-ahs (the 'j' in gracias is soft)
- jaja = HA-hah (laughter)
- junio = HOO-nee-oh (June)
- japonés = hah-poh-NEHS (Japanese)
- juego = HWEH-goh (game/play)

Note: The 'j' is stronger than English 'h' — it comes from deeper in the throat.
examples:
gracias = GRAH-see-ahs (soft j)
jaja = HA-hah (laughter)
junio = HOO-nee-oh (June)
juego = HWEH-goh (game)
joven = HO-vehn (young person)

pronunciation.title: The Spanish 'Ñ' — Like 'NY' in Canyon
pronunciation.content:
The letter Ñ represents a sound that doesn't exist in English, but you know it:

It's like the 'ny' sound in 'canyon', 'onion', or 'million'.

- niño = NYEH-nah (boy)
- mañana = mah-NYAH-nah (tomorrow/morning)
- año = AH-nyoh (year)
- cañón = kah-NYOH (canyon)
- señora = seh-NYOH-rah (madam)

To make the sound:
1. Put your tongue flat against the roof of your mouth (like for 'n')
2. Push air through the sides
3. It sounds like 'ny' in 'can-ny-on'

Practice:
- niño (boy) = NYEH-nah
- mañana (tomorrow) = mah-NYAH-nah
examples:
niño = NYEH-nah (boy)
mañana = mah-NYAH-nah (tomorrow)
año = AH-nyoh (year)
señora = seh-NYOH-rah (madam)
cañón = kah-NYOH (canyon)

exercises.question: How do you say 'Hello' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Hola' = Hello. 'Adiós' = Goodbye. 'Gracias' = Thank you. 'Buenas noches' = Good night.

exercises.question: What does '¿Cómo estás?' mean?
exercises.explanation: '¿Cómo estás?' = How are you? (informal). '¿Cómo te llamas?' = What's your name?

exercises.question: Which verb do you use to say 'I am' (identity)?
exercises.explanation: Use SER for identity: 'Soy Sergiu.' Use ESTAR for temporary states: 'Estoy cansado.'

exercises.question: Complete: '___ de Valencia.' (I'm from Valencia.)
exercises.explanation: Use SER + de: 'Soy de Valencia.' = I'm from Valencia.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Me ___ Ana.' (My name is Ana.)
exercises.explanation: 'Me llamo' = My name is. Literally 'I call myself.'

exercises.question: Complete: '___ bien, gracias.' (I'm fine, thanks.)
exercises.explanation: Use ESTAR for current state: 'Estoy bien.' = I'm fine.

exercises.question: How do you say 'Good morning' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Buenos días' = Good morning. 'Buenas tardes' = Good afternoon. 'Buenas noches' = Good evening/night.

exercises.question: What does 'mucho gusto' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Mucho gusto' = Nice to meet you. Used when meeting someone for the first time.

exercises.question: Complete: '¿De dónde ___?' (Where are you from?)
exercises.explanation: '¿De dónde eres?' = Where are you from? (informal). Use 'es' for formal: '¿De dónde es usted?'

exercises.question: Complete: 'Hablo ___.' (I speak Spanish.)
exercises.explanation: 'Hablo español.' = I speak Spanish. HABlar conjugation: yo hablo, tú hablas, él habla...

exercises.question: Which is the formal way to ask someone's name?
exercises.explanation: '¿Cómo se llama usted?' is formal. '¿Cómo te llamas?' is informal.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ encantado de conocerte.' (Nice to meet you — male speaker)
exercises.explanation: Use ESTAR: 'Estoy encantado de conocerte.' = I'm delighted to meet you. (Male speaker uses 'encantado').

exercises.question: What does 'de nada' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'De nada' = You're welcome. Used as a response to 'gracias' (thank you).

exercises.question: Complete: '___ mucho gusto.' (Nice to meet you)
exercises.explanation: 'Mucho gusto' = Nice to meet you. A common expression when meeting someone new.

exercises.question: How do you say 'See you tomorrow' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Hasta mañana' = See you tomorrow. 'Hasta luego' = See you later. 'Hasta pronto' = See you soon.
'Hello' = Hola. 'My name is' = Me llamo. Combine: 'Hola, me llamo [name].'
'Good morning' = Buenos días. 'How are you?' (informal) = ¿Cómo estás?

exercises.source: I'm fine, thank you. And you?
exercises.explanation: 'I'm fine' = Estoy bien. 'Thank you' = Gracias. 'And you?' (informal) = ¿Y tú?
'Nice to meet you' = Mucho gusto. A standard expression when meeting someone new.

exercises.source: I am from Spain. I live in Valencia.
exercises.target: Soy de España. Vivo en Valencia.
exercises.explanation: 'I am from' = Soy de. 'I live in' = Vivo en. Use SER for origin: 'Soy de [place].'
'See you later' = Hasta luego. A common farewell among friends.

exercises.source: Excuse me, what is your name?
exercises.explanation: 'Excuse me' (formal) = Disculpe. 'What is your name?' (formal) = ¿Cómo se llama usted?
'I'm tired' = Estoy cansado. 'But' = pero. 'Happy' = feliz. Use ESTAR for temporary states.
'Good night' = Buenas noches. 'Sleep well' = Duerme bien (informal command).

exercises.source: My father is a doctor and my mother is a teacher.
exercises.target: Mi padre es un médico y mi madre es una profesora.
exercises.explanation: 'My father' = Mi padre. 'is a doctor' = es un médico. 'and' = y. 'is a teacher' = es una profesora. Use SER for professions.

exercises.source: Where are you from? I am from Moldova.
exercises.explanation: 'Where are you from?' = ¿De dónde eres? (informal). 'I am from' = Soy de.

exercises.source: Thank you very much, you're welcome!
exercises.explanation: 'Thank you very much' = Muchas gracias. 'You're welcome' = De nada.
'Goodbye' = Adiós. 'See you tomorrow' = Hasta mañana.
'I speak' = Hablo. Note: 'and' becomes 'e' before words starting with 'i' (instead of 'y'): 'español e inglés.'

exercises.source: How has it been? Everything is good here.
exercises.explanation: 'How has it been?' = ¿Cómo ha ido? 'Everything is good' = Todo bien. 'Here' = aquí.

exercises.source: I work as a programmer. I study Spanish.
exercises.explanation: 'I work as' = Trabajo como. 'I study' = Estudio. Both use present tense conjugation.
